text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"---"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT NOTE :- 1) TO BE CASE HARDENED UPTO 56~60 HRC. 2) CASE DEPTH 0.8~1.2mm. 3) THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT. 4) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"The title block heat_treatment field is '---' while note N3 specifies case hardening to 56–60 HRC with a 0.8–1.2 mm case depth, creating a contradiction that could cause the shop to skip heat treatment. The designer must update the title block heat_treatment field to match note N3.","recommended_correction":"Change the title block heat_treatment field from '---' to reference the case-hardening specification in note N3."},{"rule_id":"NASA-051","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT NOTE :- 1) TO BE CASE HARDENED UPTO 56~60 HRC. 2) CASE DEPTH 0.8~1.2mm. 3) THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT. 4) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"Note N3 instructs retapping after surface treatment but does not state that holes must be tapped before coating, which is required so the plating thickness is accounted for and threads are not damaged during installation. The designer should add an explicit instruction that threaded holes are to be tapped before the I.Z.B.P. (trivalent) coating is applied.","recommended_correction":"Revise note N3 to specify that holes are tapped before coating and retapped or chased after coating."}]}
